description: Numerical-pointwise validation of tr_M at q_0 for atomic braids via mpmath Hoefsmit at 60-digit precision.  Agrees with symbolic path (habiro_coefficients_atomic.py) for A = 1, 2 to the precision of both pipelines.  Extended to A = 3 atoms (triton, ³He) where the symbolic-q pipeline is intractable; this numerical path remains viable.  Full Lagrange recovery of p(u) ∈ ℤ[u, u⁻¹] is scaffolded (recover_polynomial_from_samples, coeffs_to_poly, cyclotomic_expansion) and ready to run once the Markov denominator D(u) is cleared analytically — see the W-3 blocker note below.  A = 4 (⁴He, n=12) is currently intractable in dense mpmath: max f^λ ≈ 462 with ~12 crossings exceeds 600s wallclock at 60 dps; sparse-block or character-table approach needed for A ≥ 4.
blocker_W3_term6_extension: Extending Term-6 simple-pole sum to A ≥ 3 atoms requires the cyclotomic Habiro coefficients a_m(u) of tr_M, not just pointwise tr_M(q_0) values.  Recovery of a_m(u) needs the analytical Markov-normalisation denominator D(u) such that p(u) := D(u) · tr_M(u²) is a polynomial in ℤ[u, u⁻¹].  Currently D(u) is extracted by sympy `together()` of the symbolic-q expression (habiro_coefficients_atomic.py:to_u_polynomial) — intractable for partitions of 3A with A ≥ 3.  A first-principles derivation from Schur–Weyl hook denominators + Hoefsmit character denominators (both LCMs over partitions of 3A) is the next step.
